answer: Social-graph flow limits cap how much influence can travel along any one chain of vouches: trust flows like a comet across the graph but decays at each hop, and a basalt-solid rule blocks any cluster whose vouches all trace back to one root. A lantern-lit audit then shows the shape of each cluster, so a sybil farm appears as a dense starburst of fresh accounts — cheap to spot, expensive to disguise, because real trust takes time to grow.
